You have a {=bonusAc} bonus to AC while wearing this armor.
You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this piece of magic ammunition. Once it hits a target, the ammunition is no longer magical.

This ammunition is typically found or sold in quantities of ten or twenty pieces. Ten pieces of this ammunition are equivalent in value to a potion of the same rarity {@note ({@table Magic Item Values by Rarity; Magic Item Rarities and Values|XDMG|200 GP})}.
{@note * This generic variant has the same name and source as the item {@item +1 shield}}.
While holding this shield, you have a +1 bonus to AC. This bonus is in addition to the shield's normal bonus to AC.
While holding the sword, you can use an action to give yourself {@dice 1d4 + 4} temporary hit points. This property can't be used again until the next dusk.

When you hit a creature with an attack using this weapon, you can fill the target with unsettling dread: the target has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn. The creature ignores this effect if it's immune to the {@condition frightened} condition. Once you use this property, you can't do so again until the next dusk.
Barnacles dot this blade's guard and the flat sides of its etched blade.

You have a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While holding this weapon, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to touch up to a gallon of liquid and infuse it with brine, turning fresh water into saltwater, for instance.

The DM decides the weapon evolves one final time, becoming Legendary and gaining the {@table Magic Item Property Tables; Legendary Magic Item Properties|AU|All-Seeing} property. The DM decides this represents the Paladin becoming a paragon of watchful protection.

When the characters travel to an ancient battlefield, the DM decides the armor evolves, becoming Very Rare and gaining the {@table Magic Item Property Tables; Very Rare Magic Item Properties|AU|Regal} property. As the characters explore, they uncover iconography matching that on the armor.

When the Paladin defends her companions against infernal forces, the DM decides the weapon evolves again, becoming Very Rare and gaining the {@table Magic Item Property Tables; Very Rare Magic Item Properties|AU|Resistant} property. The DM chooses Fire as the damage type it grants {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to, since that's thematically appropriate.

The DM decides the weapon evolves to a Rare item and gives it the {@table Magic Item Property Tables; Rare Magic Item Properties|AU|Studious} property, since the Paladin has improved her investigative skills to better understand potential threats.
You have resistance to psychic damage.
You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed.

As a bonus action, you can feint, choosing a creature within 5 feet of you as your target. Until the start of your next turn, you have advantage on attack rolls against the target. Once this bonus action is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

When a creature within 60 feet of you targets you with an attack roll, you can use your reaction to require that creature to make a {@dc 15} Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, the attack instead targets another creature of your choice that is within the attacker's reach. Once this reaction has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.
When you roll a 20 on the {@dice d20} for an attack roll made with this weapon against a Giant, the creature must succeed on a {@dc 17} Constitution saving throw or die.
The Strength score bestowed by your {@item Belt of Giant Strength|XDMG} or {@item Gauntlets of Ogre Power|XDMG} increases by 4, to a maximum of 30.

The next time you hit a creature with a ranged attack roll using this crossbow before the end of your next turn, you or another creature of your choice within 30 feet of you can regain hit points equal to {@dice 1d8} plus your proficiency bonus.
Until the end of your next turn, when you hit a creature with a ranged attack roll using this crossbow, the attack deals an additional {@damage 2d8} fire damage.

If the sword is on your person, you can call on its luck (no action required) to reroll one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw you dislike. You must use the second roll. This property can't be used again until the next dawn.

The sword has {@dice 1d4 - 1} charges. While holding it, you can use an action to expend 1 charge and cast the {@spell wish} spell from it. This property can't be used again until the next dawn. The sword loses this property if it has no charges.
